Alex — great chat earlier, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps from my side: 

- Recap: demo showed how Redwood can run your document ingestion and customer-response generation pipelines with predictable latency. You mentioned production usage starting in Q3 for support automation (~50 agents) and a longer-term plan to surface L2 summaries for transactions.
- Key asks from Novapay: an invoice estimate for pilot and production, breakouts by model tier (standard vs optimized quantized), and an initial cost model we can hand to procurement.

I attached a starter pricing calculator (novapay_pricing_calculator_v3.xlsx) and a token model export (novapay_token_model.csv) that reflect the volumes you shared in the call. Highlights in the calc:
  * Pilot (3 months): ~15M total input+output tokens/month; target SLA best-effort, burst up to 400 RPS.
  * Production (year 1 target): 120M tokens/month with tighter latency SLOs and dedicated capacity.
  * Unit economics: for the optimized quantized variant we show a modeled target of ~$900 per 1M tokens, and for standard higher-fidelity models ~$2,400 per 1M tokens.

Requested next steps: can you confirm the expected/ballpark monthly token run rate for pilot versus production (I used 15M/120M as above), and confirm whether procurement needs line-item invoice (yes/no)? If helpful, I can produce a one-page invoice estimate we can route to your procurement contact.

Attachments: novapay_pricing_calculator_v3.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet), novapay_token_model.csv (CSV export - sample token counts)

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Sean — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot token volumes: the 15M/month is about right for the pilot (support + a small NLU pipeline). For production, 120M/month is the current internal target but could grow depending on feature adoption (we should model 150-200M as an upside case).
2) For procurement: yes, please provide a line-item invoice estimate we can attach to the purchase request. They like seeing monthly cost, quarterly estimate, and an annualized baseline.
3) On unit economics: $900/1M (quantized) sounds promising — can you show the delta versus the standard model and call out where savings come from (compute vs memory vs caching)?

Also looping procurement on expected billing cadence and any required PO template.

— Alex

Alex — perfect, thanks for confirming ranges. I updated the calculator and attached a one-page invoice estimate (novapay_invoice_estimate_v2.pdf) and a short notes tab in the spreadsheet that breaks the unit economics down. Quick explanation of the numbers you asked about: 

- Breakdown: savings to get to the ~$900/1M tokens are primarily compute amortization (reserved/dedicated GPU pools) + 30-40% from model quantization (lower memory bandwidth + smaller kernels) and another ~15% from caching/prefix reuse on your common prompts.
- Standard model (~$2,400/1M): higher throughput and fidelity cost, includes more robust fallbacks and no quantization; this is what we model for LLM-heavy generative tasks where hallucination risk is a concern.
- Upside scenario (150-200M tokens/month): shows step-down pricing tiers at volume bands ( >100M, >250M ) — I included projected monthly invoices for 120M and 180M lines.

Attachments: novapay_invoice_estimate_v2.pdf (PDF one-pager), novapay_pricing_calculator_v3.xlsx (updated - notes tab)

Action items I propose:
- I'll send a formal invoice estimate file your procurement team can attach (done - attached).
- Marissa from CS will map onboarding milestones and an expected runbook for pilot kick-off.
- Alex, if you can confirm the PO process, estimated sign date target, and any billing constraints (net30 vs net45), we can finalize the pilot proposal.

Best,
Sean
